answer: Every agent's vote weight is capped by a pearl it must stake, so N clones can't outvote one honest worker. Two conditions hold that: pearls are minted only after an agent's output survives random peer audits, and each audit sends the agent to wander through a fresh task in a shared meadow where duplicate submissions collapse into one lineage. Cloning costs real compute per pearl; copied history fails because audit paths diverge.
